name: Lipstick Red
lede: Lipstick Red is a strong, slightly blue red, a name that reads as ordinary language but has no documented origin.

sections.title: A name with no source
sections.body: Our library traces the swatch to the 2010 xkcd color survey and a Wikipedia entry, and finds no earlier origin [1]. It sits right on a standard name: the ISCC-NBS block called vivid red is only 0.3 units away on the CIEDE2000 scale [1]. See [[red]] and [[crimson]] for the wider family [1].

sections.title: Why names like this are hard
sections.body:
Finlay recounts a color-measurement specialist who complained that names such as barn red are not meaningful in a digital world, and asked what lipstick red means anyway [2]. The point is that the phrase is a familiar idea, not a measured one [2].

Greenfield describes red lipstick, red lights, red sports cars and red sale signs as things that catch the eye, and notes that studies show people respond to red [3]. That is the idea the name borrows, not a specific shade [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color this close appears in only 12 works, rarer than 66 per cent of the named colors [4]. In 92 per cent of those 12 it plays an accent, judged by lightness rank within each painting [4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings [4].
